newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds softer as rate authorities meet.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds softer as rate authorities meet.

text.p: *Australian bonds open slightly weaker after Treasuries unwind Friday's gains on strong data.
*RBA board meets today, balance of traded goods and services for May to be released at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).

Australian bonds were softer at the open, weighed down by a weaker U.S. Treasuries, but remained supported by expectations that today's Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) board meeting could sanction an interest rate cut.

Treasuries weakened on strong data, which while not altering expectations there would be no change in U.S. rates after the FOMC meeting finished on Wednesday, underlined expectations that U.S rates would most likely rise again in 1997, traders said.
Bonds were off by a similar amount to Treasuries, and traders said if the market was going to get bulled up on rate cut talk, it would most likely happen on Wednesday or Thursday.
But even if a rate cut was not delivered this week, traders said the market should still remain supported on the chance a cut would come later in the month.
"If you don't get it Wednesday or Thursday, then people will start looking for one after employment on (July) 10, or maybe after inflation and wages figures later in the month," one trader said.

Elsewhere, the May balance of goods and services will be released this morning. The median forecast is for a surplus of A$163 million, down on April's A$302 million surplus. Forecasts range from a A$400 million deficit to a A$500 million surplus.
Spreads narrower across the board at the open, most notably against Canadian debt. Canadian bonds weakened as the market squared up long positions ahead of Tuesday's Canada day holiday.
